# GibberishFix

> A standalone VS Code extension that fixes text typed in the wrong keyboard layout in any input — including AI-chat webviews (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor AI, Antigravity, Gemini), the editor, search boxes, and the terminal. One keystroke converts the text and, on Windows, switches the OS keyboard layout to match so the user's train of thought is never interrupted.

GibberishFix works via a clipboard-relay pipeline — the only mechanism that
penetrates extension webviews: cut the selection (or whole input) → convert →
paste → switch the OS keyboard. The auto command converts every character by
its own script (bidirectional, mixed text fixed both ways at once); the
forced commands remap only the opposite script (single direction). The
conversion core is pure and unit-tested; all VS Code/OS side effects are
isolated. ~32 non-Latin keyboard layouts are auto-generated at build time from
simple-keyboard-layouts and committed (zero runtime dependencies).

Key facts:
- Default keybindings: `Alt+Shift+L` (auto = per-character bidirectional, mixed text fixed both ways), `Alt+Shift+E` (all to English), `Alt+Shift+T` (all to target); all rebindable.
- Settings: `gibberish-fix.targetLanguage` (default `auto`, OS-detected), `switchOSKeyboard` (default true, Windows), `convertDigits` (default true), `selectAllIfNoSelection` (default true).
- Languages: 32 non-Latin scripts (Hebrew, Arabic, Farsi, Russian, Greek, Bengali, Japanese, Korean, and more); Latin layouts intentionally excluded (low practical value for layout-mixup fixes).
- Verified anchors: `tbh rumv kgau,` → `אני רוצה לעשות`; `ארוק` → `true`; mixed `vna,bv mrhl kvhu, auuv  ארוק` → `המשתנה צריך להיות שווה  true`.

## Source

- [src/extension.ts](src/extension.ts): Composition root — activation, command registration, target resolution (auto / single-detected / 2+-with-learning).
- [src/pipeline.ts](src/pipeline.ts): Pipeline — snapshot clipboard → empty-selection detection (select-all in editors, clipboard-diff heuristic in webviews) → cut → convert (auto = bidirectional, forced = single direction) → paste → switch OS keyboard → learn preferred target.
- [src/converter.ts](src/converter.ts): Pure logic — `splitRow` (bare `split(' ')`, no trim), `isSpecial`, `buildMapping` (position-by-position, graceful degradation), `buildBidiMapping` (per-character-by-script, auto mode), `convert` (ligature-aware), `detectDirection` (majority vote, used only to pick the post-convert OS keyboard).
- [src/osLayout.ts](src/osLayout.ts): Silent OS keyboard-language detection (Windows LANGID / macOS / Linux) + Windows keyboard switch.
- [src/settings.ts](src/settings.ts): Workspace config + globalState preferred-target learning.
- [src/statusBar.ts](src/statusBar.ts): Status bar item → target-language QuickPick.
- [src/layouts/types.ts](src/layouts/types.ts): The `Layout` interface.
- [src/layouts/english.ts](src/layouts/english.ts): Hand-written base/reference layout.
- [src/layouts/index.ts](src/layouts/index.ts): Generated registry — `LAYOUTS`, `getLayout`, `TARGET_NAMES`.
- [scripts/import-layouts.mjs](scripts/import-layouts.mjs): Build-time generator for the ~32 layouts.
- [scripts/switch-layout.ps1](scripts/switch-layout.ps1): Windows P/Invoke keyboard switch (bundled in VSIX).
- [test/converter.test.ts](test/converter.test.ts): 24 unit + integration tests (Node test runner via tsx).

## Optional

- [LICENSE](LICENSE): MIT (extension) + bundled simple-keyboard-layouts MIT notice (Francisco Hodge).
- Build-time layout generation: `npm run gen-layouts` regenerates `src/layouts/*`; output is committed so there is no runtime dependency on the upstream repo.
- Marketplace publisher: `yechielby`. Windows-only OS keyboard switch in v1.0; macOS/Linux planned for v1.1.
